overview: This sensor measures soil moisture indirectly by reading electrical resistance between two exposed metal prongs pushed into the soil — dry soil conducts poorly (high resistance), wet soil conducts well (low resistance). A small comparator board (often the same LM393 style used in the IR obstacle sensor) converts that into both an analog voltage (proportional to moisture level) and a simple digital threshold signal. The prongs corrode over time from constant electrolysis while powered, which is why many guides recommend only powering the probe briefly right before taking a reading rather than leaving it energized continuously.
simpleSummary: Two metal prongs that measure how wet the soil around them is.

specifications.outputType: Analog (moisture level) and digital (threshold, adjustable via onboard trimpot)
specifications.probeMaterial: Exposed nickel-plated or bare copper prongs
specifications.lifespanNote: Prongs corrode with prolonged power-on exposure to moist soil

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.function: Power input to the probe and comparator board.
pinMap.gotcha: For longer-term deployments, power the sensor only during a brief reading (e.g. via a spare digital pin acting as a switch) rather than continuously, to slow prong corrosion.

pinMap.name: AOUT
pinMap.function: Analog output — voltage varies with soil moisture level (exact direction depends on the board, but typically higher moisture reads lower resistance/voltage).
pinMap.gotcha: Absolute readings vary with soil type and prong corrosion — calibrate against 'dry air' and 'in water' readings rather than trusting raw numbers.

pinMap.name: DOUT
pinMap.function: Digital threshold output, adjustable via the onboard trimpot.

useCases.title: Automatic plant watering system
useCases.scenario: Trigger a water pump or solenoid valve when soil moisture drops below a set threshold.

useCases.title: Garden monitoring dashboard
useCases.scenario: Log moisture trends over time across multiple sensors in different plant pots.

oftenConfusedWith: Rain sensor (similar resistive-board principle, different application)
oftenUpgradedTo: Capacitive soil moisture sensors (no exposed metal prongs, no corrosion issue)
